stem: According to the graph, how many years after the survey began did the trout population reach its maximum?
stimulus: Ecologists counted the brook trout in a restored mountain pond once a month after stocking ended. The graph models the trout population $P$ as a function of $t$, the number of months since the survey began.

figure.caption: Brook Trout Population in a Restored Pond
figure.alt: A downward-opening parabola that starts at (0, 80), rises to a highest point at (18, 260), and falls back to (36, 80).

explanation: The maximum is the highest point of the curve, its vertex. Follow it down to the horizontal axis: the vertex is at t = 18. The axis counts months, but the question asks for years, so divide by 12: 18 ÷ 12 = 1.5 years.

common_errors.why: Read the vertex's t-coordinate correctly in months but did not convert to years.
Gave the maximum population, the vertex's y-coordinate, instead of the time it happens.
Converted 36 months, the end of the graph, to years instead of the vertex time.
Converted 260 instead of 18 (260 ÷ 12) after swapping the vertex coordinates.

stem: According to the model, what is the maximum average weekly earnings, in dollars?
stimulus: A labour economist modelled how the average weekly earnings of warehouse supervisors change over a career. In the graph, $x$ is years of work experience and $E$ is average weekly earnings in hundreds of dollars.

figure.caption: Average Weekly Earnings by Years of Experience
figure.alt: A downward-opening parabola that starts at (0, 6), rises to a highest point at (20, 14), and falls to (40, 6).

explanation: The maximum is the vertex, the highest point of the curve. It is at (20, 14), so the greatest value of E is 14. The vertical axis is in hundreds of dollars, so 14 hundred dollars is 14 × 100 = 1400 dollars.

common_errors.why: Read the vertex height correctly but did not convert hundreds of dollars to dollars.
Gave the vertex's x-coordinate (years of experience) instead of the earnings.
Took the x-coordinate 20 and applied the hundreds conversion to it.
Read the y-intercept (starting earnings, 6 hundred dollars) instead of the maximum.
Read the y-intercept and did not convert it either.

stem: According to the graph, what is the minimum average response time, in milliseconds?
stimulus: In a word-recognition experiment, linguists showed participants written words from 2 to 12 letters long and timed how quickly each participant decided whether the word was real. The graph models the average response time $R$, in milliseconds, as a function of word length $x$, in letters.

figure.caption: Average Response Time by Word Length
figure.alt: An upward-opening parabola that starts at (2, 575), falls to a lowest point at (7, 475), and rises back to (12, 575).

explanation: The minimum is the lowest point of the curve, its vertex, at x = 7. Go across from that point to the vertical axis. That axis starts at 400, not 0, and each gridline adds 25, so the vertex is three gridlines up: 400 + 3 × 25 = 475 milliseconds.

common_errors.why: Gave the vertex's x-coordinate (word length) instead of the response time.
Counted three gridlines above 400 but assumed each gridline is 10 instead of 25.
Assumed the vertical axis starts at 0 and counted only the three gridlines of 25.
Read the highest value shown, at either end of the graph, instead of the lowest.

stem: According to the graph, how many meters does the stone rise between leaving the sling and reaching its greatest height?
stimulus: To test how ancient slingers could hit hilltop targets, a team of experimental archaeologists filmed a replica clay sling stone in flight. The graph models the stone's height $h$, in meters above the ground, $t$ seconds after it left the sling, for the first 4 seconds of flight.

figure.caption: Height of a Replica Sling Stone
figure.alt: A downward-opening parabola that starts at (0, 4), rises to a highest point at (2, 24), and falls back to (4, 4).

explanation: You need two points. The stone leaves the sling at t = 0, so its starting height is the y-intercept: 4 meters. Its greatest height is the vertex, the top of the curve: 24 meters at t = 2. The stone rises 24 − 4 = 20 meters.

common_errors.why: Gave the maximum height measured from the ground, not the rise from the launch height.
Gave the launch height (the y-intercept) instead of the rise.
Gave the time of the vertex instead of a height.
Added the launch height to the maximum height instead of subtracting it.
Took the starting height as 2, swapping in the vertex's t-coordinate, and computed 24 − 2.
